bug_semantics: The resize command accepted the request-controlled bg background-color parameter and passed it to volume resize/rotate processing. With the ImageMagick CLI backend, crop/resize interpolated bg into an xc: shell argument and rotation interpolated it into the -background argument without shell escaping. A crafted value could break the quoted command context and execute operating-system commands as the web-server user. The path requires the resize command and ImageMagick CLI backend to be enabled and reachable.
flaw_origin: Commit 7a44e40df6411f7379df86aff6b91ac6af57af2e is the atomic public source introducer: it added bg to the accepted resize arguments and changed $bg from null to $args['bg'], feeding an already-unescaped ImageMagick command-construction sink. Its immediate parent 025b18c7ab09bfe1b1566825b79b7226f04bda12 kept $bg null and did not accept bg, so attacker input could not reach that sink. Generated build commit 16e9820fea27c86938f2b430e23195978e11aa32 records src build elFinder-2.1-8e96f65; source merge 8e96f6539f79e00a0ace0d284ecebf04d7af8c92 contains 7a44e40df6411f7379df86aff6b91ac6af57af2e as its second parent. Tag 2.1.15 predates the input path, while 2.1.16 contains the generated vulnerable build.
ai_marker: None on the BIC. The raw commit object has only author/committer nao-pon <hypweb@gmail.com>, timestamp 2016-10-01, and the human issue-oriented message '[cmd:resize] fix #1685 to enable specify bgcolor in the image rotation'; it has no AI attribution, generated-by marker, assistant trailer, or co-author trailer. Its 2016 date also predates modern generative coding assistants.
evidence: The authoritative CVE record for CVE-2026-41247 is PUBLISHED and describes request bg reaching insufficiently escaped ImageMagick CLI shell commands, with versions before 2.1.67 affected and 2.1.67 fixed; the bundled GHSA reports the same flow and is not withdrawn.

git show 7a44e40df6411f7379df86aff6b91ac6af57af2e shows the two decisive server changes: adding 'bg' to the resize command arguments and replacing $bg = null with $bg = $args['bg']. git cat-file commit confirms its sole parent is 025b18c7ab09bfe1b1566825b79b7226f04bda12 and shows no AI-related trailer or marker.

The immediate parent retains the ImageMagick command sink but does not expose request bg to it. The BIC therefore creates the source-to-sink path rather than merely moving or reformatting vulnerable code.

Commit 16e9820fea27c86938f2b430e23195978e11aa32 is the generated 2.1 build for source tip 8e96f6539f79e00a0ace0d284ecebf04d7af8c92, whose second parent is the atomic BIC. Tag containment places the generated change first in release 2.1.16; 2.1.15 lacks the bg request argument and 2.1.16 contains it.

Direct source fix bf02465a1901d2cc2dc884969dab38345c42f83f has vulnerable parent d2ce4bdc2f6b8011823bc8b19d7049d7efe475c5. It validates bg against a strict color allowlist and applies escapeshellarg to both the xc: resize input and rotation -background argument.

Release build fix 5e463d1384972dffcb736ad3c94f35af10656ca2 has parent 2b7574ca4b95e95b6639d7a865ba49ac00f32015 and carries the same remediation plus the 2.1.67 version/changelog update. Tag 2.1.66 still contains the unescaped sprintf command strings; tag 2.1.67 contains isSafeBgColor and both escapeshellarg calls. The direct fix is an ancestor of 2.1.67-src and the release fix is the peeled 2.1.67 tag commit.

The BIC predates modern generative coding assistants and contains no AI evidence; the human author identity and issue-specific commit message support human authorship. AI evidence from later remediation commits was not used to classify the BIC.
reasoning: This is a real command-injection vulnerability, not a withdrawn or rejected advisory. The smallest surviving public source commit that first makes attacker-controlled bg reach the existing shell-command sink is 7a44e40df6411f7379df86aff6b91ac6af57af2e, and its parent verifies the absence of that input path. Generated build history was decomposed back to that source member instead of treating the aggregate build as the BIC. The direct and release fixes, vulnerable parent, and 2.1.66-to-2.1.67 release boundary are all present in the clone. Classification uses only the BIC: its authorship, 2016 timestamp, raw message, and lack of AI markers support NOT_AI.
